headlines.title: Wisconsin reports 3rd measles death, as illnesses spread to the general public
headlines.description: A third person has died of measles in Wisconsin, state health officials reported Tuesday, as cases across the state soared to 920 since the outbreak began in late summer.

headlines.title: ‘Shocking’ decline seen in hep B vaccination against incurable virus, including babies with infected mothers
headlines.description: Fewer newborns are being vaccinated against hepatitis B, an incurable infection that can lead to liver disease, a large new analysis has found.

headlines.title: Too young to be vaccinated for measles? Babies face growing threats from outbreaks
headlines.description: As measles outbreaks continue to soar, a new question has emerged: Should doctors give measles shots earlier to better protect babies?

headlines.title: Israeli tech company develops AI chatbot to triage mental health and PTSD patients
headlines.description: As AI continues to spread into many different industries, one tech company developed an avatar chatbot to help triage and diagnose patients seeking mental health treatments. NBC News’ Keir Simmons spoke with the people at the forefront of the new technology.

headlines.title: Military families fight for fixes to healthcare program
headlines.description: NBC News’ Erin McLaughlin reports for the series “The Cost of Denial” about the military families who say they are receiving bills they shouldn’t - in some cases - even as they are battling terminal illness.

headlines.title: St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital Helps Young Rodeo Champ
headlines.description: Thirteen-year-old Crosslyn Mooney has always felt right at home in the saddle, riding her horse Dolly, but everything changed in 2024 when a CT scan revealed a brain tumor. But with the help of St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital, the rodeo competitor didn’t let a cancer diagnosis stop her from getting back in the saddle. headlines.title: Avoid Overindulging at Thanksgiving With These Tips
headlines.description: If you always end up feeling more stuffed than the turkey, gastroenterologist Dr. Trisha Pasricha joins TODAY with ways to avoid overindulging at Thanksgiving. Tips include eating protein and fiber first, taking a 15-minute walk after the meal, and laying down on your left side if you did overeat.
